chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from a number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Shummun, from Abdullah ibn al-Rahman, from Mis'mam, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) forbade going to the birds at night, and he said: 'Indeed, the night is a security/protection for them.'
ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling on hunting birds at night and the reasoning behind it?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-istibsar, the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) prohibits hunting birds at night, citing that darkness provides them with a natural shield of safety (aman) from predators. This ruling reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on mercy in hunting practices, ensuring that prey is not taken when its ability to escape is disproportionately hindered by environmental conditions.
